newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down in tepid trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down in tepid trade.

text.p: * Volume down to $68 million from $170.1 million
The Philippine peso ended a tad lower in tepid trade on Monday at 26.312 against the dollar from 26.311 after the Central Bank made its presence known in the market.
"The Central Bank kept calling around to check the rates," a dealer said, after the peso hit a day-high of 26.308.
Meagre dollar demand from oil companies initially gave a boost to the peso, traders said.
Traders said the Central Bank did not actually buy dollars but its presence kept the peso locked within a narrow band.
The peso averaged at 26.311 for the day from 26.304.
Trading volume thinned to $68 million from $170.1 million due to the New York holiday.
Traders also said the further drop in Treasury bill rates may not affect the peso on Tuesday.
"It was just small," a trader said. Another trader said the peso would only react if the Central Bank cut its overnight rates. -- LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
